title: Manicouagan Reservoir – The Eye of Quebec

beats.text: Type these coordinates into a satellite map, and you'll find a massive ring-shaped lake in Quebec.
A perfect circle, about seventy kilometers across, visible from orbit.
It looks like an eye, the famous eye of Quebec.
Some wonder if it hides an alien base-what could make a crater this big?
Two hundred fourteen million years ago, a meteor five kilometers wide struck here.
The impact left a multiple-ring basin, the outer rim about one hundred kilometers wide.
The inner basin filled, forming a reservoir that holds about one hundred thirty eight cubic kilometres.
So that strange ring you saw is really an ancient impact crater.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

description: Manicouagan Reservoir in Quebec is a seventy‑kilometer‑diameter annular lake formed by a meteor impact two hundred fourteen million years ago. The crater’s outer rim spans about one hundred kilometers and the lake holds roughly one hundred thirty eight cubic kilometres of water. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics.
